children: shares fell about 4% Thursday afternoon trading after the cloud company sent a contractual notice tied to its planned Project Jupiter data center in New Mexico, seeking protection if construction delays disrupt its 2028 target.
The notice was sent to a developer backed by Blue Owl Capital. Oracle is not seeking to leave the project and has said the campus remains on schedule.

Project Jupiter has encountered permitting obstacles and opposition from local groups. Bloomberg reported that a natural-gas pipeline needed for the facility has also faced delays after permit denials, adding another constraint to the development timeline.

The episode adds to scrutiny around Oracle's expanding AI infrastructure spending. The company is funding a broad data-center buildout as demand for computing capacity rises, but the New Mexico project highlights the permitting, power and construction issues that can affect large campuses.

title: Oracle Stock Plunges After Project Jupiter Warning Threatens 2028 AI Data Center Target
